<SUMMARY>The global technology landscape is experiencing rapid shifts driven by the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, which is simultaneously boosting demand for semiconductors and exposing critical supply chain vulnerabilities. Major economies are navigating intense geopolitical competition over AI chips, critical minerals, and strategic alliances. The United States continues to strengthen its technology partnerships and domestic manufacturing while imposing export controls targeting specific adversaries. The conflict in West Asia remains a significant source of instability, impacting global energy prices and supply chain security, despite a recent decline in crude oil prices. African nations are asserting greater control over their vast mineral resources, while Europe is actively engaging in US-led initiatives while also pushing back on certain restrictive measures. Military and space domains are seeing significant AI integration and quantum security concerns emerge as new threats.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>The Strait of Hormuz remains in a precarious gray zone following temporary US-Iran negotiation frameworks without lasting agreements, posing ongoing risks to global energy security. Iran's public denial of US claims regarding agreements on nuclear inspections signals potential diplomatic setbacks and escalating tensions. The reported hacking of NSA systems by Anthropic’s Mythos AI, combined with the inherent national security risks posed by quantum computing's code-breaking capabilities, highlights a severe and evolving threat to cyber defenses. Tight packaging and testing capacity continues to be a critical bottleneck in the global semiconductor supply chain, impacting IC design firms across Europe, the Americas, and Asia. Further expansion of US export controls, such as the proposed MATCH Act, risks exacerbating divisions in the global compute ecosystem and prompting European pushback, potentially fracturing strategic alliances.</EWS>
<EXEC>The global AI chip market is experiencing significant growth and strategic reorientation. Micron's earnings exceeded expectations, positioning it as Wall Street's new margin king ahead of Nvidia and Meta, and driving a broader $400 billion AI chip stock rally alongside Qualcomm's optimistic forecasts. Qualcomm has unveiled new AI data center chips and systems, with Meta signing on as its first major hyperscale customer, and projects $15 billion in data center chip sales by 2029. SK Hynix plans a US listing, contributing to the AI trade stability. Anthropic is expanding its AI data center capacity overseas, establishing new roles in Japan and Australia. Thailand expects record $366 billion in exports this year, largely due to boosted electronics demand from AI, and its stock market is thriving from its role in AI infrastructure. South Korea's KOSPI surged 6% as chip stocks rebounded. Singapore-based Video Rebirth, backed by $80 million from investors including AMD and Hyundai Motor, is developing a world model to create real-time interactive 3D environments. In Africa, the data center market is projected to reach $8.76 billion in investments by 2031, with South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, and Egypt emerging as strategic hubs. China's Z.ai is reportedly closing the frontier gap in AI development and plans a dual listing following the Anthropic shutdown.</EXEC>
<LITHO>
**Asia:**
JCET is establishing a new plant in Shanghai dedicated to advanced chip packaging, which aims to bolster China's semiconductor capabilities. Hanmi Semiconductor has debuted its FC Bonder 3.5, designed to power AI chip packaging expansion. The global semiconductor packaging and testing sector faces increasing competition, marked by TSMC signing a 10-year advanced packaging collaboration agreement with Amkor in Arizona, while ASE concurrently races to expand its own capacity. IC design firms in Taiwan are facing tighter-than-expected packaging and testing capacity, identifying it as a pressing supply chain bottleneck.

**Europe:**
Europe is scaling up 6-inch photonic chip production for mass manufacturing. X-FAB is developing its Erfurt site in Germany into a center for microsystems technology. Applied Materials has introduced new systems engineered to accelerate DRAM and advanced packaging processes specifically for AI chips. Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma visited Washington to oppose the US-proposed MATCH Act, a bill that would restrict Chinese chipmakers from accessing Western semiconductor equipment, including older-generation deep ultraviolet tools from ASML that are currently accessible to China. IC design firms in Europe report that tight packaging and testing capacity remains a significant supply chain bottleneck.

**Americas:**
TSMC and Amkor have entered a 10-year agreement to expand advanced packaging collaboration in Arizona. Nokia has announced a significant expansion of its US semiconductor advanced test and packaging operations in Pennsylvania, aiming to bolster AI growth. Apple and Intel chips signal a strategic bet on US manufacturing. IC design firms in the US are reporting that tight packaging and testing capacity represents a more severe bottleneck than anticipated in the supply chain.</LITHO>
<REE>
**Asia:**
Japan is accelerating the development of All-Solid-State Batteries (ASSBs) and enhancing its supply chain buildout, supported by government subsidies totaling $660 million. Flagship Minerals received $5.8 million from the sale of its Thai lithium play, redirecting its focus towards Chilean gold and Canadian copper assets. Auckland-based Atomic Tessellator is leveraging AI to synthesize alternatives to rare earth elements, with its $13 million raise backed by the CIA's venture capital arm.

**Africa:**
President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria has called for a united African approach to developing the continent’s solid mineral resources, advocating for an end to raw mineral exports and urging industrialization with value addition. The US-Congo cobalt deal is exerting new pressure on China’s mineral supply chain dominance, with the US Department of War and Department of Energy implementing plans to bolster critical mineral supply chains, recognizing minerals as geopolitical leverage points. President Donald Trump has secured a major win against China in the African rare earth minerals race. Zimbabwe is scrutinizing Chinese lithium mining operations. Congo's cobalt production is shaping global markets amid a strategic shift.

**Europe:**
Greece is actively promoting five strategic Critical Raw Materials projects, seeking to capitalize on investment opportunities arising from the European Union’s Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA) implementation mechanism. Scientists have confirmed that Hina’s commercial sodium-ion battery technology, which uses cheap and abundant materials, matches the performance and production quality of Tesla’s lithium-ion batteries.

**Americas:**
REalloys Inc. announced a private placement of common stock for approximately $100 million. Paladin Energy Ltd, an Australian company, completed its 2026 winter drilling program at the Patterson Lake South (PLS) project in Saskatchewan, Canada, identifying a new high-grade uranium discovery. Flagship Minerals, after selling its Thai lithium assets for $5.8 million, is focusing on its 2.1 million ounce Chilean gold asset and Canadian copper spin-out plans.</REE>
<GEO>
**Asia:**
The ongoing AI race and expanding export controls are segmenting the global compute ecosystem. Alibaba has filed a lawsuit against the US Defense Department to remove its designation as a 'Chinese military company'. Expanding export controls are being considered to slow China's AI progress. MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan met with Jacob Helberg, US Under Secretary of State and host of the Pax Silica initiative, to discuss strengthening supply chain security in key technology sectors.

**Europe:**
The EU, Germany, the Netherlands, and Greece have joined Pax Silica, a US-led initiative aimed at securing the AI supply chain across chips, critical minerals, energy, and compute. The Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma visited Washington to oppose the US MATCH Act, indicating European pushback against Washington’s chip war policies. The US secured the Netherlands for its Pax Silica Alliance.

**Americas:**
The US Congress has affirmed strong support for Taiwan, welcoming Han Kuo-yu, president of Taiwan's Legislative Yuan, to Washington. The US has secured the Netherlands as a key partner in the Pax Silica Alliance, a strategic chip alliance.</GEO>
<MILITARY>
**Asia:**
Auckland’s Atomic Tessellator, backed by the CIA’s venture capital wing, is using AI to synthesize alternatives to rare earth elements, a development with potential geopolitical implications for strategic resource independence.

**Europe:**
WISeKey’s WISeSat.Space is reinforcing its European secure satellite infrastructure roadmap by participating in FOSSA Systems’ latest financing round.

**Americas:**
WISeKey and SEALSQ have established Quantisimo Corp. as a special purpose vehicle, signaling advancements in quantum-secure technologies. Anthropic’s Mythos AI reportedly hacked the NSA’s most sensitive systems in a matter of hours. Quantum computers are identified as posing serious national security risks due to their code-breaking capabilities. The US Senate voted 50-48 to approve an Iran War Powers Resolution, directing President Donald Trump to withdraw US forces from hostilities against Iran, representing a symbolic rebuke of current policy.</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>The global AI-driven technological surge is fundamentally reshaping economic and geopolitical landscapes, with a renewed focus on securing critical supply chains for semiconductors and minerals. The intensifying US-China competition is evident in export control debates and strategic resource acquisition, particularly in Africa. Europe's engagement with the US Pax Silica initiative while simultaneously challenging restrictive trade measures underscores a complex balancing act to secure its own digital sovereignty. The ongoing conflict in West Asia remains a primary geostrategic flashpoint, influencing global energy markets and highlighting the critical role of military-technological advancements and the inherent risks of AI in national security. The convergence of AI innovation, supply chain vulnerabilities, and geopolitical tensions defines the current international environment, demanding vigilant monitoring of these interwoven dynamics.</CONCLUSION>
<INDIA>Indian stock markets, including the Sensex and Nifty, surged significantly as global oil prices cooled below $73 per barrel, bolstering investor confidence. India's water sector is experiencing a surge in stock valuations, with companies like Shakti Pumps and VA Tech Wabag seeing jumps up to 45% in a month, driven by increased government funding for water infrastructure and growing demand for cooling from data centers. S. Krishnan, Secretary of MeitY, met with Jacob Helberg, US Under Secretary of State and host of the Pax Silica initiative, to discuss strengthening supply chain security in key technology sectors. India is actively seeking semiconductor investments and multilateral funding at the Pax Silica summit in Washington D.C., aiming to leverage the US's $250 million seed fund to bolster its semiconductor manufacturing and design capabilities. The Indian government may soon acquire a stake in Sarvam AI.</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>The conflict in West Asia, notably President Donald Trump's war with Iran, continues to shape global energy security and geopolitics, with discussions indicating it is linked to saving America's debt market by driving up energy prices and global demand for dollars. Crude oil prices have plummeted 42% from their April peak of $126 to below $73 a barrel, signaling a return to pre-conflict levels after months of turmoil caused by the Strait of Hormuz closure and war damage. However, the Iran War contributed to accelerated inflation in May, pushing up prices. US-Iran talks have produced a temporary negotiation framework but no lasting agreement on the status of the Strait of Hormuz, leaving the waterway in a precarious gray zone between war and peace. Iran's Foreign Ministry publicly denied US claims of an agreement to allow international inspectors to examine its nuclear facilities, raising questions about recent peace talks. A rescued US Air Force pilot reported encountering a highly coordinated Iranian drone swarm network before his F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down over Iran in April. Middle East tensions have worsened naphtha procurement for nearly 70% of surveyed Japanese firms, raising supply concerns and production costs. Pakistan is attempting to leverage its position as a mediator in the Iran conflict. Israel has established a new AI Directorate.</WEST_ASIA>
<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The coming period will likely be characterized by intensified efforts to localize critical technology supply chains, especially in AI chips and critical minerals, as geopolitical competition drives further decoupling. The ongoing US-Iran standoff will remain a primary determinant of global energy market volatility and will continue to strain international relations, with potential for escalation despite recent oil price declines. The strategic alliances formed around initiatives like Pax Silica will be crucial in shaping the future architecture of the AI compute ecosystem. Military applications of AI and quantum technologies will accelerate, necessitating urgent development of both offensive and defensive capabilities, alongside international frameworks for responsible use. Nations heavily reliant on specific exports, such as Thailand on electronics, may face increased economic vulnerability, compelling diversification efforts. The interplay between technological advancements and geopolitical maneuvering will require continuous, adaptive intelligence assessments to anticipate disruptions and identify opportunities for strategic advantage.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
